answer: Use a juniper-like trust root: every agent identity locks a bond that vests only after many epochs of honest, peer-audited work, and vouching power grows only from confirmed history. A newcomer earns nectar, small fees and reputation, only by doing verifiable tasks under peer scrutiny, while its bond stays locked. Cloning an identity yields a pearl with no history: no vouching power, no fees, and a fresh bond to lock again. An attacker wanting a thousand votes must fund a thousand bonds and wait out a thousand vesting periods, while one detection slashes the cluster's escrow.
